progress.method: A node earns no theorem-progress credit for a statement alone. A proof node earns 70% for an isolated kernel proof, 85% after API review, and 100% only after a downstream consumer compiles. Infrastructure earns 40% when its definitions compile, 70% after mathematical sanity checks, and 100% after a real downstream consumer compiles. The headline is the weighted sum.

nodes.title: Divisor-line-bundle dictionary
nodes.summary: Construct the Picard group of line bundles and identify divisor classes with line bundles on a smooth curve. The checked affine path proves integral closedness and Dedekind order compatibility for locally standard-smooth relative curves over a field and constructs actual overlap line-bundle isomorphisms on proper smooth curve intersections. On one fixed common Dedekind affine overlap, the equality-induced inverse-ideal restriction maps satisfy genuine triple transitivity. Canonical pseudofunctor transport from an explicit pairwise model to Mathlib's chosen pullback, its further-pullback naturality, and a real arbitrary-divisor consumer now compile. The chosen triple overlap maps canonically to the actual affine triple chart intersection, and its restrictions through all three chosen pairwise faces agree with their affine-intersection comparison maps. Each pulled chosen-overlap Hom is identified with the corresponding pairwise inverse-ideal model Hom on that triple intersection, and the raw chosen-overlap cocycle is equivalent to the model-Hom cocycle. The chosen-overlap/full-descent comparison makes the reconstructed principal cocycle effective with the global trivial line bundle as witness. Tower coherence comparing those three pairwise models with directly constructed common-affine comparisons, relation to the normalized transition Iso, full arbitrary-divisor descent effectivity, object separation, rational normalization, and Picard surjectivity remain open.

challenge.informal: For the geometric order system of a smooth proper integral curve, prove the full invertible-sheaf/Picard comparison and identify divisor classes with the scheme Picard group. Checked code proves these two outputs are equivalent to the complete dictionary. Affinely, it constructs the actual tensor-additive tilde line bundles, a canonical Picard embedding with exact principal kernel, an unconditional range equivalence, and a full equivalence under exactly the reverse tensor-unit/local-rank-one comparison.
challenge.recommended_route: Import the companion chart, localization, and descent modules. For each concrete base-field affine `appLE` map, prove the normality implication isolated by `AffineChart.SmoothRelativeCurveNormality`; the checked field-base dimension theorem and `dedekindOrderCompatibilityOfSmoothRelativeCurveNormality` then supply the chart order compatibility. Construct `PicardIso.PullbackMonoidalData` to transport the exact chart kernel and range equivalence to `Pic(U)`. Same-chart coefficient agreement on a principal open gives localized inverse-ideal equality, common-extension equality, and the actual restriction isomorphism through `localLineBundleRestrictIsoOfCoeffEq`. Across two charts on a proper smooth curve over a field, prove that same mapwise normality implication for `f.appLE` on `U₁ ⊓ U₂` and use `localLineBundleRestrictionIsoOnProperSmoothCurveIntersectionOfNormality`; the checked API supplies separatedness, dimension at most one, the Dedekind instance, and the actual arbitrary-divisor isomorphism. `localLineBundleRestrictionIsoOnProperCurveIntersection`, `localLineBundleRestrictionIsoOnIntersection`, `localLineBundleRestrictionIsoOnCommonAffineOpen`, and `localLineBundleRestrictionIsoOfCommonMap` are the progressively more general proper, separated-scheme, chosen-subopen, and explicit-ring entry points; the classical-localization coefficient route remains only a specialization. The pairwise chosen-pullback transport and diagonal normalization are checked; prove triple-cocycle coherence for the normalized transitions. Then prove ordinary module effectivity, tensor additivity, and coherent principal triviality. Zero triviality then makes `L(-D)` an explicit inverse to `L(D)`, constructing the divisor and class maps without `TensorInverseComparison X`. Under coherent principal triviality and object separation, a global trivialization already makes every chart restriction principal. The witness-level `TrivialDescendedLineBundleHasGlobalPrincipalWitness` is checked equivalent to `TrivialLineBundleDetectsPrincipal`, so the genuine missing geometric step is rational normalization or global rational-section compatibility for the explicit cocycle. Checked code identifies principal detection with exact principal kernel; exactness gives the range equivalence, and surjectivity gives the full divisor-class/Picard equivalence. Separately prove the global tensor-inverse comparison only to fill the stronger dictionary that compares every invertible sheaf. The remaining cover-wide cocycle and effectivity predicates are compiled conditional boundaries subsumed by the unchanged A3 Challenge. The weighted product formula remains the separately registered A2 prerequisite and is not imported by these affine/local A3 modules.

nodes.title: The X_0(N) moduli point attached to rational prime torsion
nodes.summary: Construct the split rational cyclic subgroup generated by a torsion point, its intrinsic divisor subgroups and degeneracy maps, and quotient raw Weierstrass data by checked admissible variable changes. Genuine finite-locally-free closed subgroup schemes, base change, constant cyclic order, and a split Gamma_0 datum from exact torsion now compile. Every split rational cyclic subgroup now canonically supplies the constant finite-flat carrier and inclusion whose point homomorphism is exactly subgroup inclusion; cyclic-generator choice is confined to the splitness isomorphism, and raw rational Gamma_0 data is a checked consumer with exact point range. A genuine Tau Ceti abelian variety plus a multiplicative comparison of its rational points supplies the narrow Weierstrass group-scheme interface and feeds the exact-torsion consumer. The concrete projective cubic has a checked bijective rational-point comparison. Its Z-nonzero homogeneous localization is explicitly equivalent to the affine Weierstrass polynomial ring, the localized equation ideal is prime, and the quotient chart is integral. The affine equation quotient is identified with this localized chart, and the canonical D_+(Z) open of every actual field pullback is an open immersion with exact range. Graded coefficient extension constructs P^2_L -> P^2_K from a proved irrelevant-ideal inclusion, preserves the coordinates and cubic equation, and gives the checked D_+(Z) away-chart square. Coordinate-chart pushout squares and a three-chart cover prove that the ambient projective-plane square is a pullback, yielding the canonical P^2 base-change isomorphism with both projection laws. Its checked cubic consumer identifies the mapped zero locus with the pullback of the original zero locus. The remaining geometric-integrality boundary is restriction of that ambient isomorphism to an ambient-compatible reduced cubic base-change isomorphism, the chart-to-canonical-open isomorphism, and density; the checked comparison consumes these data through Tau Ceti and the split Gamma_0 constant-order endpoint. Then construct the cubic group law and multiplicativity, E/C, and the coarse X_0 classifying point.

theorem cyclotomic_locallyPrimaryPseudoUnitKummerReciprocityPrinciple

challenge.informal: For every prime p at least 5 and every inverse-cyclotomic degree-p Kummer extension of Q(zeta_p), if the canonical radicand has p-divisible finite divisor and is a p-th power in the completion at the unique prime above p, its finite Kummer/Frobenius product is one on every nonzero integral principal denominator outside that prime. The destination already proves both radicand hypotheses for an everywhere-unramified extension, compares Kummer and Artin coordinates, clears fractional denominators, and removes the cyclotomic-prime factor.
challenge.recommended_route: Prove one-sided Kummer reciprocity for a locally-primary pseudo-unit, first for integral denominators coprime to the radicand and p; then extend across the finite bad set. The Kummer/Frobenius comparison and prime-complement denominator clearing are already checked in the destination. Alternatively prove the same integral vanishing via the conductor-one cyclic Artin reciprocity theorem.
